title: LoopScript
description: Validates an i-SASE LoopScript (pure YAML). A LoopScript defines the ordered phases, gates, and escalation policies for a SASE execution loop.

schema.description: Schema identifier for the LoopScript artifact type.

phases.description: Ordered list of phases that make up the execution loop.

id.description: Unique identifier for this phase within the loop.

actions.description: Ordered actions the agent performs during this phase.

gate.description: Gate that must be satisfied before advancing past this phase.

description.description: Human-readable description of what the gate enforces.

strict.description: If true, gate failure creates a blocking CRP instead of being retried.

gate-command.description: Optional shell command that must exit 0 to pass the gate. Run via Bash; mandatory when defined.

on-uncertainty.description: Action or strategy to apply when uncertainty is detected during this phase (e.g., create-crp).

escalation.description: Escalation policies that govern when and how the loop creates CRPs.

description.description: Human-readable description of the threshold and what triggers it.

action.description: Action to take when the threshold is crossed (e.g., create-crp).

scope-creep.description: Policy for detecting and escalating work outside the BriefingPack scope.

description.description: Human-readable description of what counts as scope creep.

action.description: Action to take when scope creep is detected (e.g., create-crp).

structural-triggers.description: Deterministic CRP triggers (API/schema change, security, scope deviation, etc.) — see engineering skill for the full taxonomy.

action.description: Action to take when the trigger fires (e.g., create-crp).

mode.description: Whether the resulting CRP pauses execution (blocking) or is logged and continues (deferred).

n-version.description: N-version programming configuration for redundant execution of critical phases.

enabled.description: Whether n-version redundant execution is enabled.

count.description: Number of independent versions to execute in parallel.
